sources.citation: Tuggy, David. 'Silabación y acento en el náhuatl'. SIL México web page (Familia náhuatl), accessed 2026-09-17.
sources.note: General Nahuatl only: 'El acento normal del náhuatl cae en la penúltima sílaba, o sea, las palabras del náhuatl generalmente son graves. Sin embargo, en algunas variantes del náhuatl hay situaciones en las que el acento recae en la última o antepenúltima sílaba.' No variety is named; not specific to npl.

sources.citation: SIL México, listing 'Náhuatl del sudeste de Puebla [npl]' (mexico.sil.org/es/resources/search/code/npl), Internet Archive copy 2016-10-26.
sources.note: Catalogue only: 14 literacy booklets (1985-2001, San Sebastián Zinacatepec) plus Reed 1995; no grammar, phonology, dictionary or orthography statement is listed for npl. Live SIL pages under /resources are could not be reached by automated download.

sources.citation: Itlajtol Totajtsi Dios. El Nuevo Testamento en el náhuatl del valle de Tehuacán [npl]. Wycliffe Bible Translators, 2011 (electronic ed. 2023), 591 pp.
sources.note: No alphabet/orthography note anywhere in the PDF (a full-text search for stress/accent acento/alfabeto/sílaba/ortograf = 0). As primary data: of 124,381 polysyllabic tokens, ~92% carry no accent mark; of 10,256 accented non-Spanish tokens, 5,409 are antepenultimate (tlaltíkpaktli, tlájtoli, májtlaktli, pakílistli, tékitki, amatlajkuíloli, tlájtolteh), 4,571 final (ijkó, ijkuakó, milák, ayakmó, opé, kiné, oyá, amó, okimák), 241 penult (mostly loans/i-vowel hiatus). This is my tabulation of orthographic practice, not a published statement.

sources.citation: Reed, Ralph T. 1995. Some not so 'san'guine discourse particles in Southeastern Puebla Náhuatl narratives. SIL-Mexico Workpapers 11: 53-66.
sources.note: Nothing about Nahuatl stress (only 'intonation and stress' of English 'just' in an illustrative aside, p. 53). Footnote 1 locates SPN in the valley ESE of Tehuacán. Examples are in the SIL practical orthography, which writes acute accents on some words (ijkuakó, ayakmó, opé) but the convention is not explained.

sources.citation: MacSwan, Jeff. 1997. A Minimalist Approach to Intrasentential Code Switching: Spanish-Nahuatl Bilingualism in Central Mexico. PhD dissertation, UCLA (front matter + ch. 2 'Literature review' incl. sect. 2.5.3 'The Nahuatl Language', + ch. 3), from the author's old ASU site via the Internet Archive.
sources.note: Nothing. Sect. 2.5.3 (pp. 94-105) treats word order (SVO data from five San Sebastián Zinacatepec texts), dialect classification, courses and orthography; 'stress' occurs only in unrelated English senses. Data are Southeast Puebla Nahuatl of San Sebastián Zinacatepec, written without systematic accent marks.

sources.citation: Cuentojteh de tochih iwan koyotl / Cuentos del conejo y el coyote, en náhuatl de Zinacatepec, Puebla y en español. ILV, edición de prueba, diciembre 1985 (redactor Fidel González Alejandro); Kwentojteh de San Sebastián Zinacatepec, Puebla No. 1 (ILV 1987); Siembra y cosecha (ILV npl literacy booklet).
sources.note: Primary texts only; no 'aclaraciones sobre el alfabeto' page. The orthography marks non-penultimate stress with an acute: final (okimák, amó, ijkuaké/ijkuakó, opé) and antepenultimate on absolutive nouns in -le/-tle (kómale, ténextle, totómoxtle, tiánkistle, nextámale, ápistle, tláole); no rule is stated.
